records.issue_text: [BUG] The negative webauthn-form assertions in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey are wrapped in try/catch(Exception) that treats any failure (including the assertion itself failing) as the expected outcome, so the assertions can never fail. MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue()) throws NoSuchElementException when the form is absent (caught, 'expected'), but when the webauthn form IS wrongly present it throws AssertionError — which is also caught by catch (Exception nsee) and silently swallowed, so a regression that re-enables the passkey button for a user without passkeys during re-authentication passes CI. The only verification the test exists to provide is a no-op in both try blocks.
records.rationale: In the shown test, the `catch` only catches `Exception` (`} catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }`). A failing Hamcrest `MatcherAssert.assertThat(...)` throws `AssertionError` (an `Error`), not an `Exception`, so it would NOT be swallowed by this catch. Therefore, if the webauthn form is wrongly present, `assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue())` would throw `AssertionError` and the test would still fail, contradicting the finding’s claim that the assertions “can never fail.”

records.issue_text: [BUG] Both call sites that set up conditional passkey UI in UsernamePasswordForm were inverted from `user == null` to `user != null`, so the initial-login page (user not yet identified) no longer calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm and the conditional-UI passkey prompt disappears from the combined username/password form on first login. Realms whose browser flow uses UsernamePasswordForm lose WebAuthn conditional-UI autofill on the ordinary first-login page: the login-then-passkey path that previously triggered `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() -> fillContextForm(context)` (which sets ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI for the unidentified-user branch) now requires user != null, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is false exactly on the screen where the old code enabled it; users with discoverable passkeys get no passkey prompt until after they type a username/password.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'WebAuthn elements not available' check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey is a try/catch that swallows its own AssertionError, so it passes regardless of whether the webauthn form is present. When driver.findElement succeeds and the element IS present, assertThat(element, nullValue()) throws AssertionError which is caught by catch(Exception), and the fail() call is never reached — the test never fails, so a regression that renders the webauthn button during password re-authentication for a user without passkeys goes undetected; the same broken pattern is repeated a second time later in the same test (~line 240) for the post-prompt=login page.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Changing the fillContextForm gate from `user == null` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` (which requires user != null) removes conditional-UI/passkey setup from the first-login path of flows built on UsernamePasswordForm alone. Realms whose browser flow uses the combined UsernamePasswordForm execution (no preceding UsernameForm) no longer initialize WebAuthn conditional mediation on the initial username+password page, so users with discoverable passkeys lose the silent autofill/autologin on first visit and are forced to type username+password; only re-auth (user already set) gets the passkey UI. The diff's own tests only cover the re-auth path and the organization flow where the user is pre-set, so the regression on the unidentified-user path of UsernamePasswordForm is untested.
